brief: Describes how a surface should look, as declared colours, scalars and textures and one fragment expression, and has the engine write the shader.
detail: You declare what the material takes, TakesColor, TakesScalar and TakesTexture, and write the body once as @out = expression, where the expression uses the declared names, numbers, the arithmetic operators, a whitelist of functions and the fragment builtins @normal, @position, @uv, @lambert and @color. ToWGSL has the engine transpile it to a complete shader and refuses a bad description with a message naming the offender. ParamsFrom and TexturesFrom flatten the values a scene binds. Authoring needs no GPU: only rendering the material wants hardware, and this class never renders.
receiver:
o1 = new stzMaterialMaker
o1.TakesColor(:base)
o1.TakesScalar(:glow)
o1.ForEachFragment('{ @out = base * (1.0 + glow * @normal.y) }')
